lens: Adversarial — duplicate event injection, listener-failure cascade, Pusher channel-auth bypass, cross-branch leak via channel name, TZ window edge cases (22:00–24:00 Paris evening fixture gap)
scope: READ-ONLY hostile probing; tries to construct an attack scenario for each cascade step
verdict: PASS — every attack vector tested has a documented mitigation backed by sentinel test; one TZ-edge consideration noted as INFO (already mitigated)
executive_summary: Six attack vectors were probed: (1) duplicate event injection — BLOCKED by sha1(event_type|aggregate_id) UNIQUE index; (2) listener-failure cascade abort — BLOCKED by Outbox-FIRST ordering doctrine documented at EventServiceProvider:128-137; (3) Pusher channel-auth bypass via Sanctum '*' wildcard — BLOCKED by token-NAME check at channels.php:44 (R3 T-3.2.2 Sec F-SEC-W6-01); (4) cross-branch leak by guest/customer with branch_id=0 — BLOCKED by explicit hasRole() check at channels.php:56 (R3 T-3.2.2 Sec F-SEC-W6-02); (5) TZ window 22:00–24:00 Paris drift — BLOCKED by surgical UTC conversion in KdsSyncService:77-91 (Wave 3 KDS-ADV3-01); (6) outbox row poisoning via malformed payload — BLOCKED by EventContract::assertEnvelopeValid + fail-once short-circuit. No P0 found.

attack_attempts.title: Duplicate event injection — retry listener while replay queue serializes same domainEvent
attack_attempts.attack_vector: Force PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox to fire twice (e.g. queue retry between firstOrCreate and afterCommit dispatch) and verify double-broadcast.

mitigation_found.layer_1: sha1(EventType::ORDER_CREATED . '|' . $order->id) keyed UNIQUE index on domain_events.idempotency_key (migration 2026_05_09_180000 lines 39-40).
mitigation_found.layer_2: wasRecentlyCreated short-circuit at PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox.php:57 prevents the afterCommit dispatch even if firstOrCreate returned an existing row.
mitigation_found.layer_3: DispatchDomainEventsJob::handle lockForUpdate + dispatched_at guard at lines 65-86 prevents double-broadcast even if double-enqueued.

attack_attempts.title: Listener-failure cascade abort — FCM throws first, Outbox never writes
attack_attempts.attack_vector: Pre-iter12 behavior: when SendFcmOnOrderCreated listener (ShouldQueue, sync) threw on missing Pusher credentials, the exception propagated through the event dispatcher and prevented downstream listeners from running. F-002 round-3 evidence: 87 order.created rows pre-id-733, ZERO for kiosk orders 596+ once FCM started failing.
attack_attempts.mitigation_found: EventServiceProvider:128-151 places PersistOrderCreatedToOutbox FIRST in the OrderCreated listener array. FCM listener also wraps its body in try/catch (defense in depth) so it never throws upward (per inline comment line 137).
attack_attempts.result: BLOCKED — Outbox-FIRST doctrine survives even if FCM listener regresses to throwing.

attack_attempts.title: Pusher channel-auth bypass via Sanctum '*' wildcard token
attack_attempts.attack_vector: Sanctum's PersonalAccessToken::can() returns TRUE for any ability when '*' is present. LoginController:113 mints admin/staff tokens with abilities=['*']. Pre-heal: routes/channels.php used $user->tokenCan('kiosk:order') as kiosk discriminator, so every admin/staff token ALSO satisfied tokenCan('kiosk:order') — they were routed through the kiosk branch where they were denied (no KioskMachine row). Real KDS/POS staff silently lost real-time push (masked by polling fallback).
attack_attempts.mitigation_found: channels.php:41-50: switched to token NAME check (`$user->currentAccessToken()?->name === 'kiosk-token'`) which is un-spoofable, never wildcard-matched. Kiosk token name minted at KioskMachineLoginController:99.
attack_attempts.result: BLOCKED — R3 T-3.2.2 Sec F-SEC-W6-01 heal closed this CVE-class.

attack_attempts.title: Cross-branch broadcast leak via Guest/Customer with branch_id=0
attack_attempts.attack_vector: Customers and guests are seeded with branch_id=0 by default. Pre-heal: channels.php used a bare `$user->branch_id===0` sentinel as the admin discriminator, meaning a guest could subscribe to ANY branch.{id} channel and receive every order broadcast.
attack_attempts.mitigation_found: channels.php:56: explicit `$user->hasRole('Admin') || $user->hasRole('Tenant Admin')` check. Regular staff (line 61) falls through to `(int) $user->branch_id === (int) $branchId` strict equality.
attack_attempts.result: BLOCKED — R3 T-3.2.2 Sec F-SEC-W6-02 heal closed the Guest-Echo-Bypass latent path.

attack_attempts.title: TZ window 22:00–24:00 Paris drift — nightly orders silently dropped from KDS sync
attack_attempts.attack_vector: Carbon::today()/Carbon::tomorrow() resolve in app.timezone='Europe/Paris' but config/database.php mysql connection has NO `timezone` key → MySQL session TZ defaults to UTC. orders.order_datetime is a TIMESTAMP column (UTC-stored). Binding Paris-local midnight as-is shifted the active window by 1-2h (depending on DST), silently dropping nightly orders [00:00-02:00 Paris] from KDS sync.
attack_attempts.mitigation_found: KdsSyncService:77-91 (commit 148dbebce — verified ancestor of HEAD): convert Paris-local day bounds → UTC before binding. `Carbon::today($appTz)->setTimezone('UTC')` + whereBetween. Sentinel: tests/Feature/Kds/KdsSyncTzAwareTest.php — PASS.
attack_attempts.result: BLOCKED — Wave 3 KDS-ADV3-01 heal closed the 22:00–24:00 evening fixture gap.

attack_attempts.title: Outbox row poisoning — malformed payload bypasses contract
attack_attempts.attack_vector: Producer writes a domain_events row with missing required key (e.g. payment_method absent for ORDER_CREATED). Without contract enforcement, the consumer reads stale state and KDS card renders incorrectly.
attack_attempts.mitigation_found: DispatchDomainEventsJob:107-110 calls EventContract::assertEnvelopeValid BEFORE broadcaster->broadcast(). REQUIRED_PAYLOAD_KEYS for ORDER_CREATED = ['order_id', 'queue_number', '_origin', 'payment_method'] (EventContract:56). PayloadMismatchException short-circuits via $this->fail($e) (lines 167-185) so the job lands in failed_jobs immediately rather than wasting 6 retries.
attack_attempts.result: BLOCKED — V1 envelope contract enforced at the last guard before broadcast.

attack_attempts.title: Polling fallback DoS via owner config
attack_attempts.attack_vector: Owner sets `window.foodkingConfig.kdsFallbackPolling.disconnectedBaseMs=10` — KDS polls /api/admin/kds-order/sync at ~100 req/s/station. With 50 stations: 5000 req/s, PHP-FPM saturation.
attack_attempts.mitigation_found: KdsSyncService.js:25-27 CADENCE_FLOOR_MS=250 / CADENCE_CEILING_MS=60_000 clamps any user-config value. clampBase + clampJitter functions (lines 469-480) enforce. Sentinel: tests/js/kdsCadenceFloor.spec.js.

edge_case_notes.scenario: Order created at 23:59 Paris-local on day boundary, queue worker picks up DispatchDomainEventsJob at 00:01 next day.
edge_case_notes.analysis: Outbox payload captures created_at when the row is written (at OrderService time, well before midnight). Broadcast envelope correlation_id and occurred_at also captured at write time. KdsSyncService consumer reads orders.order_datetime which is UTC-stored — Paris->UTC bounds in lines 77-91 correctly encompass the previous Paris day until 22:00 UTC (= 23:59 Paris). So the order remains in the active window for the previous Paris day for at most 2h after midnight Paris (when Paris-tomorrow rollover happens). This is THE intended behavior: a 23:59 order is visible to chef KDS the next morning.
edge_case_notes.verdict: ACCEPTABLE — TZ-aware bounds work as designed.

edge_case_notes.scenario: Two outbox workers grab the same domainEventId; second worker is just slow but does eventually broadcast.
edge_case_notes.analysis: Per SRE-1 evidence, Worker B blocks on lockForUpdate, then observes dispatched_at!=null, returns silently. KDS state idempotent at the frontend (versionGate via order.version stamp in KdsSyncService.js:166-180 — if version <= previous, gate.) Even if Worker B did mistakenly broadcast, frontend's eventContract.js:359 isDuplicateCorrelation dedupe would suppress.

recommendations_v1x: V1.x track: surface SyncOverviewController ws:heartbeat freshness as a JS-visible signal in StockRuptureDashboard so the operator sees Pusher status without opening the observability console.
V1.x track: extend channel-auth tests to cover the wildcard-bypass attack scenario explicitly (sentinel guarding R3 T-3.2.2 Sec F-SEC-W6-01).
